profile.headline: Software Engineer II for OpenJDK at Microsoft
profile.summary:
I Graduated with my master's in computing systems from the College of Computing at Georgia Institute of Technology in May '22. My undergraduate CS degree was focused on Artificial Intelligence and Information Internetworks at Gatech.

I am interested in Software Development and Data Science/Analytics. In summer 2021, I had a returning internship at the same Amazon Web Services (AWS) team. There, I created a new framework to help internal teams easily validate their service's traffic/billing metrics. The previous summer with AWS, I learned how to work with a team to implement and integrate code within a large codebase, and I squashed several bugs within that codebase. My first internship with Georgia Tech Research Institute focused on artificial intelligence and data analytics. There, I honed my skills in research to develop a deep-learning model which classifies executables as a specific malware family or clean.

Portfolio: http://tiny.cc/joshmjaffe

Software: Linux/bash, git, Java, C, SQL, Python, Ruby, JavaScript, Html, CSS, Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS)

positions.title: Software Development Engineer Intern
positions.description:
Strengthened confidence in metering system (classifying ~2.5 billion data transfers/ second) by:
- Enabling testing framework to emit 5 new metrics/ alarms for new traffic types
- Expanding testing framework to test in 6 new regions
Squashed 10+ existing bugs which prevented code from building resources in new regions

positions.title: Undergraduate Machine Learning Researcher
positions.description:
Implemented successful 10-layer convolutional neural network using Keras, tensorflow, Python
Attained 94%-98% accuracy in labeling portable executables as one of 20+ malware families
Extracted tens of thousands of real-world portable executables for testing and training model
Researched 10+ academic papers and sources on neural networks and malware classification

volunteerExperiences.description:
Lead volunteers in refurbishing abandoned/donated bikes for cheap resale to students
Organized transition to COVID safe club participation and bike sales

Starter bikes is a great way for students and Tech faculty to get used, donated, or abones bikes for cheap (usually $30-$70). We help them pick out a bike and teach them how to repair it (our help is free) until it is safe to ride. At this point, the bike can be sold.

Led and managed group of canvassers/door knockers out in the field. Mobilized disfranchised voters to get to the polls in GA

Worked as a canvasser to register people to vote in Georgia (before December 7th, the deadline to register for the senate run offs).

Then, consulted as a door knocker for BPAC (Black Progressive Action Coalition) to help mobilize disenfranchised voters in GA to get to the polls.
